note: Shared validation vectors for the #3963 (S4) abort sentinel. Evaluated against the real validators by modules/agent-factory/agent/src/control-abort-sentinel.test.ts (validateAbortSentinel) and modules/agent-factory/agent-worker-image/tests/test_abort_sentinel.py (validate_abort_sentinel). Both runtimes must agree on every vector. This replaces source-text constant matching, which could not have caught the boolean-version divergence: Python honoured `version: true` because True == 1 while TypeScript rejected it, and the constants matched the whole time. Contains no credential.

vectors.name: valid
vectors.note: the ordinary accepted case: version-exact and bound to this run and generation

vectors.name: valid_without_a_reason
vectors.note: an operator need not supply a reason; null must not become the string "null"

vectors.name: reason_whitespace_collapsed
vectors.note: the reason reaches a GitHub comment, so newlines cannot break its layout

vectors.name: reason_non_string_becomes_null
vectors.note: str()/String() of an object would put "{'injected': True}" in front of an operator

vectors.name: version_boolean_true
vectors.note: the divergence root found: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so this validated there and was rejected by TypeScript's strict !==. The schema version must be an actual integer.

vectors.name: generation_boolean_true
vectors.note: same bool/int hazard on the generation: JSON true must not read as generation 1

vectors.name: version_newer
vectors.note: exact match, not a minimum: a newer payload may narrow the abort's scope in a field this reader does not know to look at

vectors.name: version_older
vectors.note: both halves ship in one image, so a version mismatch means something is genuinely wrong

vectors.name: version_string
vectors.note: a stringly-typed version is not this schema

vectors.name: different_run
vectors.note: the failure this binding exists to prevent: honouring it would delete an unrelated live run's queue message

vectors.name: superseded_generation
vectors.note: generation is equality, not "at least": an abort aimed at an attempt that already ended must not finalize its replacement

vectors.name: future_generation
vectors.note: a generation this run never reached is not this run's abort

vectors.name: generation_string
vectors.note: inside the document the generation is a number; the decimal-string form is only accepted for the env-supplied binding

vectors.name: generation_fractional
vectors.note: a generation counts registrations; a fraction is not one

vectors.name: run_id_missing
vectors.note: an unbindable document cannot be validated, so it is not an abort

vectors.name: run_id_blank
vectors.note: blank is not a run identity

vectors.name: run_id_wrong_type
vectors.note: a numeric run id would compare unequal anyway, but the type check is the documented rule

vectors.name: command_id_missing
vectors.note: the command id is the evidence correlator; without it the abort cannot be traced to an accepted command

vectors.name: command_id_blank
vectors.note: blank is not a command id

vectors.name: command_id_wrong_type
vectors.note: required fields are type-checked rather than coerced

vectors.name: requested_at_missing
vectors.note: the request time is part of the evidence record

vectors.name: requested_at_blank
vectors.note: blank is not a timestamp

vectors.name: empty_object
vectors.note: no fields at all

vectors.name: not_an_object_list
vectors.note: JSON parsers happily return a list; field access on it would raise in the one place that must not raise

vectors.name: not_an_object_string
vectors.note: a bare string is not a sentinel, however suggestive its content

vectors.name: not_an_object_number
vectors.note: a bare number is not a sentinel

vectors.name: not_an_object_null
vectors.note: JSON null parses successfully and must still mean no abort

vectors.name: not_an_object_true
vectors.note: JSON true parses successfully and must still mean no abort

generation_binding_vectors.name: trailing_garbage
generation_binding_vectors.note: root's second finding: Number.parseInt('1junk', 10) returns 1, binding the run to a generation the input never expressed, while Python's int() raises on the same bytes

generation_binding_vectors.name: pep515_underscores
generation_binding_vectors.note: Python's int('1_0') is 10 and JavaScript's Number('1_0') is NaN — divergence in the other direction, so both sides reject it explicitly

generation_binding_vectors.name: explicit_plus
generation_binding_vectors.note: int('+3') is 3 in Python; the shared rule is bare ASCII digits only

generation_binding_vectors.name: non_ascii_digits
generation_binding_vectors.note: int('٣') is 3 in Python and Python's \d matches it; the shared rule is ASCII digits only
